blocks.x: It’s hard to think of a time when beards weren’t fashionable, but there was a time when they were maybe too fashionable. The so-called “millennial beard” emerged in the late aughts and early 2010s, as hipsters traded the clean-shaven look of the ‘90s and early aughts for considerably more facial hair. The whole thing then became a little too ‘Epic Bacon’ if we're being honest, and also took the beard-care product market in a specific Lumberjack-Edison-Bulb-Core direction. Think packaging featuring burly woodsmen, Vikings and faux wood grain on the labels.

Thankfully, there’s an entirely new generation of men's grooming products simply focused on clean and effective formulas. These days, you really can have a great beard without becoming a Beard Guy. Just be normal about it, and take care of the thing. Invest in a good trimmer, and respect that dandruff and tangles and funk are real, and that you'll need a maintenance routine. What does that look like? Well, that's what we're here for. Below, the four key stages of keeping your beard beautiful, and all the products we like best for doing so.

The consensus here at GQ, and pretty much everywhere else on the Internet, is that the Philips Norelco Multigroom is the best beard trimmer money can buy. Better still, it handles head and body hair, too. For me, the 7000 Series, which I’ve been using for about five years, is the sweet spot. The pricier 9000 Series comes with a few additional attachments, but the 7000 already includes more than most people will ever need. It’s also lighter than the 9000, making it ideal for tossing in your travel kit. For customization, power and battery life, it hits every mark.

blocks.x: You may have seen the term “zero-gap” before. It simply means the blades are aligned to cut as close to the skin as possible. That makes a zero-gap trimmer great for creating crisp lines and cleaning up edges, though the uninitiated should trim carefully: it’s also easier to nick your skin, or clip an ear.

Bevel’s trimmer was designed by Black men for Black men. Built with curly and Afro-textured hair in mind, it pairs a powerful 6,000-rpm motor with up to eight hours of battery life. (It also happens to be one of the best-looking trimmers around, so you won’t mind leaving it out on the bathroom counter.) Just one word to the wise—it purposefully doesn’t come with comb guards or a pile of attachments. This is a precision tool made for shaping longer beards, carving clean lines and keeping your edges sharp.
Series 9 All-in-One Beard and Body Trimmer

The Norelco is the better value, and already does just about everything, but Braun’s All-in-One Series 9 is for the guy who wants to do everything with slightly more control. The biggest upgrade is its locking precision wheel, which lets you move between 52 length settings without constantly digging through your Dopp kit for a different guard.

AutoSense technology adjusts the motor to your beard’s density, and PowerBoost gets it through especially thick patches. Dedicated detailing, contouring and precision-shave heads make it particularly good for crisp lines, smooth fades and other work that requires a steadier hand than simply mowing everything down to a number two. The charging stand and handsome case completes a handsome setup built for anyone who takes beard maintenance seriously.

blocks.x: Wahl is an American grooming OG. The company invented the first practical electric hair clipper in 1919, and remarkably remains family-owned. It introduced the corded Peanut in 1992, and more than three decades later, it’s a genuine modern classic. Working barbers prize it because it’s a compact little workhorse, delivering dependable power and consistent cuts for years on end.

It looks a little funny, but that stubby, rounded shape is all part of the charm (Wahl leans into the name with a peanut shell texture.) It looks as though it would sit in the palm of your hand, but it’s actually ergonomically designed to rest between your fingers for greater agility around cheek lines, moustaches and other tight spots. Wahl also makes a cordless Peanut, but devotees will tell you the original corded model still has more muscle.

Philips Norelco has this particular market cornered. The OneBlade trims, shaves and edges, and can even handle body grooming with the right attachment. You might think this kind of gadget should be gimmicky, but it’s actually widely beloved, easy to use and really affordable.

The cartridge-style blade is gentle on sensitive skin and makes it easy to carve clean lines and tidy your neckline (or even squeeze in a quick full shave). Add the body-grooming attachment, and you can get your manscaping on, too. Its compact size and light weight also make it an excellent travel trimmer when you don’t want to lug your usual setup around.
